## Overview

The **representativeness** of `r herb` measures how much of the
[Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) —
the official checklist of Brazilian plants and fungi — is already held in the
collection. A higher coverage percentage reflects a more comprehensive herbarium.

```{r kpi-boxes}
htmltools::tags$div(
  class = "kpi-row",
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-green",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        paste0(d$coverage_pct, "%")),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label", "Overall FFB coverage")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-blue",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_in_herb)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label", "FFB species represented")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-gray",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_ffb_total)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label", "Total FFB accepted species")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-purple",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_families)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label", "Families represented")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-amber",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_genera)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label", "Genera represented")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
  class = "kpi-box kpi-ocean",
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-value",
    paste0(d$endemic_coverage_pct, "%")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-label",
    "Brazilian endemic coverage")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
  class = "kpi-box kpi-red",
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-value",
    scales::comma(d$n_type_specimens)
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-label",
    "Type specimens")
  )
)
```

## Coverage by Major Taxonomic Group

The chart below shows the percentage of FFB species that are represented in
`r herb` for each group Values below 100% indicate that some species in that
group are still missing from the collection.

```{r plot-group, fig.height=4}
ggplotly(d$plots$group, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r table-group}
DT::datatable(
  d$group_rep,
  colnames = c("Group", "Species in herbarium", "Total in FFB", "Coverage (%)"),
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
    "Table 1. Coverage by group."
  ),
  options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "t")
) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    "coverage_pct",
    background = DT::styleColorBar(c(0, 100), "#b7e4c7"),
    backgroundSize = "98% 88%",
    backgroundRepeat = "no-repeat",
    backgroundPosition = "center"
  )
```

## Family-level Coverage {.tabset}

### Best-covered families

The following chart ranks the **20 best-represented families** (with at least
5 FFB species) by their coverage percentage. Families approaching 100% coverage
are those the herbarium represents most comprehensively.

```{r plot-family-best, fig.height=6.5}
ggplotly(d$plots$family_best, tooltip = "text")
```

### Least-covered families

These are the 20 families with the **lowest coverage** among those with at least
10 FFB species. They represent the most critical collecting priorities —
large families where most species are not yet in the herbarium.

```{r plot-family-worst, fig.height=6.5}
ggplotly(d$plots$family_worst, tooltip = "text")
```

### All families table

```{r table-family-all}
DT::datatable(
  d$family_rep,
  colnames = c("Family", "Species in herbarium", "Total in FFB", "Coverage (%)"),
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  extensions = "Buttons",
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
    "Table 2. Complete family-level coverage summary."
  ),
  options = list(
    pageLength = 20,
    dom = "Bfrtip",
    buttons = c("copy", "csv", "excel"),
    order = list(list(3, "desc"))
  )
) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    "coverage_pct",
    background = DT::styleColorBar(c(0, 100), "#b7e4c7"),
    backgroundSize = "98% 88%",
    backgroundRepeat = "no-repeat",
    backgroundPosition = "center"
  )
```

## Geographic Coverage

### Map of herbarium coverage by Brazilian state

The choropleth map shows the percentage of FFB species known from each state
that are represented in `r herb`. Darker states have higher coverage. Hover
over a state for details.

```{r leaflet-map, fig.height=5}
tryCatch({
  states_sf <- geobr::read_state(year = 2020, showProgress = FALSE)
  states_sf  <- dplyr::left_join(states_sf, d$state_rep, by = "abbrev_state")
  states_sf$coverage_pct[is.na(states_sf$coverage_pct)] <- 0

  pal <- leaflet::colorNumeric(
    palette = "YlGn",
    domain = c(0, 100),
    na.color = "#f5f5f5"
  )

  leaflet::leaflet(states_sf) %>%
    leaflet::addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>%
    leaflet::addPolygons(
      fillColor = ~pal(coverage_pct),
      fillOpacity = 0.75,
      color = "white",
      weight = 1.2,
      label = ~paste0(name_state, ": ", coverage_pct, "% covered"),
      labelOptions = leaflet::labelOptions(
        style = list("font-size" = "12px"),
        sticky = FALSE
      ),
      popup = ~paste0(
        "<div style='font-size:13px;'>",
        "<b>", name_state, "</b><hr style='margin:4px 0;'>",
        "Coverage: <b>", coverage_pct, "%</b><br>",
        "Represented species: ", scales::comma(n_in), "<br>",
        "FFB species: ", scales::comma(n_ffb),
        "</div>")
    ) %>%
    leaflet::addLegend(
      pal = pal,
      values = ~coverage_pct,
      title = "Coverage (%)",
      position = "bottomright"
    )
}, error = function(e) {
  htmltools::p("Map could not be rendered: ", e$message,
               style = "color: #6c757d; font-style: italic;")
})
```

## Coverage by Phytogeographic Domain

Each of Brazil's six phytogeographic domains (biomes) is represented differently
in `r herb`. The bar chart shows the percentage of FFB species occurring in each
domain that are held in the collection. Note that species occurring in multiple
domains are counted in each.

```{r plot-domain, fig.height=4.5}
ggplotly(d$plots$domain, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r table-domain}
DT::datatable(
  d$domain_rep,
  colnames = c("Domain", "In herbarium", "Total in FFB", "Coverage (%)"),
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
    "Table 3. Coverage by phytogeographic domain."
  ),
  options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "t", order = list(list(3, "desc")))
) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    "coverage_pct",
    background = DT::styleColorBar(c(0, 100), "#b7e4c7"),
    backgroundSize = "98% 88%",
    backgroundRepeat = "no-repeat",
    backgroundPosition = "center"
  )
```

## Endemism Coverage

This comparison highlights how well the herbarium represents
Brazilian endemic species relative to non-endemic species.

```{r plot-endemic, fig.height=4}
ggplotly(d$plots$endemic, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r endemic-summary}
DT::datatable(
  data.frame(Category = c("Endemic species", "Non-endemic species"),
             Species_represented = c(d$n_endemic_in_herb, d$n_non_endemic_in_herb),
             FFB_total = c(d$n_endemic_ffb, d$n_non_endemic_ffb), 
             coverage_pct = c(d$endemic_coverage_pct, d$non_endemic_coverage_pct)
  ),
  colnames = c("Category", "Species represented", "Total in FFB", "Coverage (%)"),
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
    "Table 4. Coverage by species endemism."
  ),
  options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "t", order = list(list(2, "desc")))
) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    "coverage_pct",
    background = DT::styleColorBar(c(0, 100), "#b7e4c7"),
    backgroundSize = "98% 88%",
    backgroundRepeat = "no-repeat",
    backgroundPosition = "center"
  )
```

## Type Collections and Nomenclatural Importance

The herbarium contains
**`r scales::comma(d$n_type_specimens)`**
type specimens representing
**`r scales::comma(d$n_type_taxa)`**
accepted taxa.

```{r plot-types, fig.height=4.5}
ggplotly(d$plots$types, tooltip = "text")
```

The chart above shows the proportion of represented species
that are backed by type material within each major taxonomic group.
Groups with higher values indicate stronger nomenclatural representation.

## Type-rich Families

The families below contain the largest numbers of accepted taxa represented by type specimens in the herbarium.

```{r plot-type-families, fig.height=6}
ggplotly(d$plots$type_families, tooltip = "text")
```


## Represented Species List

```{r table-in-herb}
display_cols <- c("group", "family", "genus", "taxonName",
                  "scientificNameAuthorship")
display_cols <- display_cols[display_cols %in% names(d$taxon_in_herb)]

DT::datatable(
  d$taxon_in_herb[, display_cols, drop = FALSE],
  colnames = c("Group", "Family", "Genus",
                 "Taxon name", "Authorship")[seq_along(display_cols)],
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  extensions = "Buttons",
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
    paste0("Table 6. All ", scales::comma(d$n_in_herb),
           " FFB species represented in ", herb, ".")
  ),
  options = list(
    pageLength = 20,
    dom = "Bfrtip",
    buttons = c("copy", "csv", "excel"),
    scrollX = TRUE
  )
)
```
